subject.title: Feature: Auto session split when approaching context window limit

question: Should OpenClaw add a core, config-backed context-pressure session rollover policy, and what default-off config and durable handoff contract should it use?
rationale: The code path is core session state plus public configuration and channel delivery; automation cannot safely choose thresholds, default behavior, privacy/authorization semantics, or overlap with existing compaction/reset policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core default-off rollover
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved core lifecycle policy that layers beside compaction and reset, with explicit config, durable handoff, delivery preservation, and tests.

options.title: Fold into TTL lifecycle design
options.body: Use the open TTL/max-lifetime issue as the single broader lifecycle design and treat token-pressure rollover as one trigger in that policy.

options.title: Keep compaction/reset only
options.body: Decline automatic session splitting for now and document compaction, memory flush, and manual or time-based reset as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Design core default-off rollover
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved core lifecycle policy that layers beside compaction and reset, with explicit config, durable handoff, delivery preservation, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal spans session lifecycle, config compatibility, compaction, and related docs.
